E01.answer: The Bali Governor's 2025 circular for foreign tourists asks visitors to honour the sanctity of temples (pura), sacred objects (pratima) and religious symbols. Foreign tourists are prohibited from entering the inner sanctums of a temple (Utamaning Mandala and Madyaning Mandala) except to pray, and then only wearing Balinese traditional dress and not while menstruating. Polite, appropriate clothing is required at sacred places.
E01.why_it_matters: Temple courtyards are active places of worship for the local Hindu community, not tourist attractions. Entering restricted areas or dressing inappropriately is experienced as disrespect toward the community's religion.
recommended_actions: Stay in the outer courtyard unless you are there to pray.
Wear clothing that covers shoulders and knees; a sarong and sash (selendang) are commonly required.
Follow signs and instructions from temple caretakers (pemangku) or staff.
Do not enter while menstruating if you plan to go into the inner areas.

E02.answer: Berdasarkan Undang-Undang Nomor 22 Tahun 2009 (Pasal 106 ayat 8), setiap pengemudi dan penumpang sepeda motor wajib mengenakan helm yang memenuhi standar nasional Indonesia (SNI); Pasal 291 ayat 1 mengatur pidana kurungan paling lama 1 bulan atau denda paling banyak Rp250.000 bagi pengemudi yang tidak memakainya. Surat Edaran Gubernur Bali 2025 juga mewajibkan wisatawan asing memiliki SIM internasional atau nasional yang berlaku, menggunakan kendaraan sewaan yang layak, mematuhi rambu, dan tidak membawa penumpang melebihi kapasitas.
E02.why_it_matters: Kecelakaan sepeda motor adalah penyebab cedera yang umum bagi pendatang, dan berkendara tanpa SIM dapat membatalkan asuransi perjalanan. Mematuhi aturan melindungi Anda dan pengguna jalan setempat.
recommended_actions: Selalu gunakan helm yang terkunci talinya, dan pastikan penumpang juga memakainya.
Bawa SIM yang berlaku sesuai jenis kendaraan (bagi wisatawan asing, SIM Internasional beserta SIM negara asal).
Sewa kendaraan hanya dari usaha penyewaan resmi dan periksa rem serta lampunya.
Jangan membonceng lebih dari satu penumpang.

E03.answer: Bali Governor Regulation No. 47 of 2019 on source-based waste management requires waste to be handled as close to its source as possible, starting with households and businesses separating organic and inorganic waste. Implementation is organised with villages (desa/kelurahan) and customary villages (desa adat). Collection schedules and sorting rules in Canggu may be set locally and are not included in this knowledge base.
E03.why_it_matters: Separating waste at home makes composting and recycling possible and reduces the amount sent to overloaded landfills.
recommended_actions: Separate organic waste (food scraps, leaves) from inorganic waste (plastic, paper, glass) in your accommodation.
Ask your host or property manager how waste is collected in your area and on which days.
Never dump or burn rubbish on the roadside, in rice fields or in rivers.

E04.answer: Saat Nyepi, Bali menjalankan Catur Brata Penyepian: tidak menyalakan api/lampu, tidak bekerja, tidak bepergian, dan tidak bersenang-senang. Menurut PHRI Bali, tamu hotel tidak boleh keluar area hotel selama 24 jam (pukul 06.00 hingga 06.00 WITA keesokan harinya), suara harus dijaga dan penerangan sangat terbatas. Penerbangan dari dan ke Bali dihentikan selama 24 jam. Hotel tetap melayani tamu di dalam area hotel. Tanggal Nyepi berubah setiap tahun.
E04.why_it_matters: Nyepi adalah hari suci untuk introspeksi bagi umat Hindu Bali dan diikuti seluruh pulau. Keluar rumah, membuat kebisingan, atau menyalakan lampu terang mengganggu pelaksanaan Nyepi, dan pecalang berpatroli di jalan.
recommended_actions: Pastikan tanggal Nyepi tahun ini kepada pengelola akomodasi jauh hari dan hindari jadwal penerbangan pada hari itu.
Siapkan makanan dan kebutuhan sehari sebelumnya; sebagian besar toko tutup.
Tetap berada di dalam akomodasi selama 24 jam penuh, kecilkan suara dan musik, serta tutup tirai pada malam hari.
Tanyakan kepada pengelola layanan apa (makanan, penerangan) yang tersedia selama Nyepi.

E05.answer: The 2025 circular obliges foreign tourists to respect Balinese customs, traditions, arts and culture, especially during ceremonial processions. Processions often move along public roads, and traffic may be paused or diverted by local volunteers (pecalang) while they pass.
E05.why_it_matters: Ceremonies are religious acts for the participants. Interrupting, rushing or treating them as a show can cause offence.
recommended_actions: If a procession blocks the road, stop, wait patiently and follow pecalang instructions; do not honk or squeeze through.
Watch quietly from the side and do not walk through or in front of people who are praying.
Ask before photographing participants up close, and never use flash in their faces.

E06.answer: The 2025 circular requires foreign tourists to wear polite, reasonable and appropriate clothing, especially at sacred places, tourist attractions and public places. The circular does not list specific garments; swimwear is generally expected only at the beach or pool.
E06.why_it_matters: Most of Canggu is a residential community, not only a resort. Walking through villages, shops or warung in swimwear or shirtless is commonly seen as disrespectful.
recommended_actions: Put on a shirt and cover-up when leaving the beach or pool, including when riding a scooter.
Dress more conservatively in villages, markets, government offices and near temples.
Carry a sarong so you can cover up when you pass a temple or ceremony.

E07.answer: Peraturan Gubernur Bali Nomor 97 Tahun 2018 membatasi kantong plastik, polisterina (styrofoam), dan sedotan plastik sekali pakai di seluruh provinsi, berlaku bagi pelaku usaha, pasar, dan masyarakat. Surat Edaran 2025 bagi wisatawan asing juga melarang penggunaan plastik sekali pakai seperti kantong plastik, styrofoam, sedotan plastik, dan minuman dalam kemasan plastik sekali pakai.
E07.why_it_matters: Sampah plastik menyumbat sungai, saluran irigasi (subak), dan pantai, termasuk di sekitar Canggu, sementara kapasitas TPA di Bali terbatas.
recommended_actions: Bawa tas belanja, botol minum, dan (jika perlu) sedotan yang dapat digunakan ulang.
Isi ulang air minum di stasiun isi ulang atau akomodasi alih-alih membeli botol plastik kecil.
Tolak kantong plastik saat berbelanja dan bawa wadah sendiri untuk makanan bungkus bila memungkinkan.

E08.answer: Surat Edaran 2025 mewajibkan wisatawan asing menginap di akomodasi berizin, mematuhi ketentuan khusus di setiap daya tarik wisata dan aktivitas, serta membayar pungutan wisatawan asing sebesar Rp150.000 sebelum keberangkatan atau selama berada di Bali. Pungutan ini berdasarkan Peraturan Daerah Provinsi Bali Nomor 6 Tahun 2023 dan berlaku sejak 14 Februari 2024; pembayaran dilakukan melalui portal resmi Love Bali. Wisatawan yang belum membayar dapat tidak dilayani di daya tarik wisata. Penukaran mata uang asing hanya di penyelenggara resmi atau bank.
E08.why_it_matters: Penyewaan jangka pendek tanpa izin di permukiman menjadi sumber keluhan warga serta masalah pajak dan keselamatan, sementara pungutan digunakan untuk pelindungan budaya dan lingkungan Bali.
recommended_actions: Pesan akomodasi yang berizin dan terdaftar; tanyakan kepada pemilik jika ragu.
Bayar pungutan hanya melalui portal resmi Love Bali (lovebali.baliprov.go.id) untuk menghindari situs pihak ketiga yang mematok harga lebih tinggi.
Tukar uang hanya di money changer resmi atau bank, dan utamakan pembayaran dengan rupiah atau QRIS.

E09.answer: The 2025 circular requires foreign tourists to stay in licensed accommodation, follow the specific rules of each attraction and activity, and pay the Bali foreign tourist levy of IDR 150,000 before departure or while in Bali. The levy is based on Bali Provincial Regulation No. 6 of 2023 and has applied since 14 February 2024; payment is made through the official Love Bali portal. Tourists who have not paid may be refused service at tourist attractions. Foreign currency should be exchanged only at licensed money changers or banks.
E09.why_it_matters: Unlicensed short-term rentals in residential areas are a source of local complaints and tax and safety issues, and the levy funds the protection of Bali's culture and environment.
recommended_actions: Book accommodation that is licensed and registered; ask the host if unsure.
Pay the levy only through the official Love Bali portal (lovebali.baliprov.go.id) to avoid overpriced third-party sites.
Exchange money only at licensed money changers or banks, and prefer paying in rupiah or with QRIS.

E10.answer: Many villas in Canggu sit inside residential neighbourhoods (banjar) where families live, work early and hold ceremonies. This is general etiquette advice, not a verified local rule: keep music and voices low at night, avoid loud parties, and ask your host whether the neighbourhood has specific rules about noise or gatherings. Specific banjar or Desa Adat Canggu rules are not included in this knowledge base.
E10.why_it_matters: Late-night noise from villas is a frequently reported source of friction between visitors and residents. Asking first shows respect and avoids misunderstandings.
recommended_actions: Ask your villa host or property manager about house rules and any neighbourhood (banjar) rules before inviting guests.
Keep music low, especially at night and during ceremonies nearby.
Introduce yourself to neighbours if you are staying long-term.

E11.answer: Small palm-leaf offerings with flowers (canang sari) are placed daily in front of homes, shops and on pavements. This is general etiquette advice, not a regulation: try not to step on or kick offerings, and walk around them where you can. Deliberately stepping on fresh offerings is seen as disrespectful.
E11.why_it_matters: Canang sari are daily acts of devotion by Balinese Hindu families. Treating them carefully is a simple, visible sign of respect.
recommended_actions: Look down when walking past shopfronts and gateways, and step around offerings.
Do not move, take or photograph offerings in a way that disturbs them.
If you accidentally step on one, a brief apology is enough; ask a local if you are unsure.

E17.answer: The 2025 circular prohibits foreign tourists from driving or riding under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs. Violations of the circular can be followed up with sanctions or legal processes under the applicable laws.
E17.why_it_matters: Canggu's narrow roads are shared with pedestrians, children and ceremonies. Impaired riding endangers residents as well as yourself.
recommended_actions: If you plan to drink, leave the scooter at home and use a registered ride-hailing service or taxi.
Do not let friends ride after drinking; arrange transport for the group in advance.

E18.answer: Surat Edaran 2025 melarang wisatawan asing mengucapkan kata-kata kasar, berperilaku tidak sopan, atau membuat keributan, baik secara langsung maupun di media sosial, serta bersikap agresif terhadap aparat, pemerintah, masyarakat lokal, maupun sesama wisatawan. Wisatawan asing juga dilarang bekerja atau berbisnis tanpa dokumen resmi dari instansi berwenang.
E18.why_it_matters: Komunikasi yang tenang dan tidak konfrontatif sangat dihargai; kemarahan di depan umum membuat semua pihak kehilangan muka. Video viral perilaku buruk wisatawan pernah berujung pada pemeriksaan dan deportasi.
recommended_actions: Jika terjadi perselisihan (misalnya soal harga atau kecelakaan motor), tetap tenang, pelankan suara, dan minta bantuan pengelola akomodasi atau warga yang Anda percaya untuk menengahi.
Jangan mengunggah video atau komentar yang menghina warga atau aparat.
Jangan bekerja atau menjual jasa tanpa visa dan izin yang sesuai.

H01.answer: The 2025 circular prohibits foreign tourists from climbing trees that the Balinese community considers sacred. It also asks visitors to honour religious symbols and sacred objects. Large trees wrapped in black-and-white checked cloth (poleng) or with offerings at their base are commonly treated as sacred.
H01.why_it_matters: Sacred trees and shrines are part of the community's religious life. Climbing them or using them as photo props is seen as desecration, and some past incidents involving tourists led to purification ceremonies and deportations.
recommended_actions: Do not climb, sit on or lean on trees or structures wrapped in poleng cloth or with offerings around them.
Do not stand on shrines, altars or temple walls for photos.
If unsure whether a place or object is sacred, ask a local before touching it or taking photos.

H05.answer: Small palm-leaf offerings with flowers (canang sari) are placed daily in front of homes, shops and on pavements. This is general etiquette advice, not a regulation: try not to step on or kick offerings, and walk around them where you can. Deliberately stepping on fresh offerings is seen as disrespectful.
H05.why_it_matters: Canang sari are daily acts of devotion by Balinese Hindu families. Treating them carefully is a simple, visible sign of respect.
recommended_actions: Look down when walking past shopfronts and gateways, and step around offerings.
Do not move, take or photograph offerings in a way that disturbs them.
If you accidentally step on one, a brief apology is enough; ask a local if you are unsure.

H06.answer: Many villas in Canggu sit inside residential neighbourhoods (banjar) where families live, work early and hold ceremonies. This is general etiquette advice, not a verified local rule: keep music and voices low at night, avoid loud parties, and ask your host whether the neighbourhood has specific rules about noise or gatherings. Specific banjar or Desa Adat Canggu rules are not included in this knowledge base.
H06.why_it_matters: Late-night noise from villas is a frequently reported source of friction between visitors and residents. Asking first shows respect and avoids misunderstandings.
recommended_actions: Ask your villa host or property manager about house rules and any neighbourhood (banjar) rules before inviting guests.
Keep music low, especially at night and during ceremonies nearby.
Introduce yourself to neighbours if you are staying long-term.

H09.answer: The 2025 circular requires foreign tourists to wear polite, reasonable and appropriate clothing, especially at sacred places, tourist attractions and public places. The circular does not list specific garments; swimwear is generally expected only at the beach or pool.
H09.why_it_matters: Most of Canggu is a residential community, not only a resort. Walking through villages, shops or warung in swimwear or shirtless is commonly seen as disrespectful.
recommended_actions: Put on a shirt and cover-up when leaving the beach or pool, including when riding a scooter.
Dress more conservatively in villages, markets, government offices and near temples.
Carry a sarong so you can cover up when you pass a temple or ceremony.
